as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="note" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#444444;spacingLeft=4;" value="<b>What actually drives Automatic play.</b> The server permits exactly one controlling session per character, and in this build that session is driven by the <b>rule-based Monster Fighter inside agent-client</b> — hunting, looting and restocking from the <code>[npcs.worker]</code> block configToml.js writes, with no LLM in the loop. The model agent is still wired up (LLM tab, llmValidation.js, the Thoughts panel) but settingsStore.js reads every workerKind back as <code>fighter</code>, so nothing can select it; translate.js is the one live caller left of an LLM backend. <b>Automatic</b> — main.js brings proxy.js up on loopback, then agent.js spawns agent-client pointed at the relay instead of the real server; the relay forwards byte for byte and tees every frame to /mirror, so the spectator scene in the iframe watches without taking a second session. <b>Manual</b> — no relay and no agent-client: server.js hands the iframe the real web client, which dials the game server itself under your own Google session." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="110" width="1100" x="1300" y="2120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: What actually drives Automatic play. The server permits exactly one controlling session per character, and in this build that session is driven by the rule-based Monster Fighter inside agent-client — hunting, looting and restocking from the [npcs.worker] block configToml.js writes, with no LLM in the loop. The model agent is still wired up (LLM tab, llmValidation.js, the Thoughts panel) but settingsStore.js reads every workerKind back as fighter, so nothing can select it; translate.js is the one live caller left of an LLM backend. Automatic — main.js brings proxy.js up on loopback, then agent.js spawns agent-client pointed at the relay instead of the real server; the relay forwards byte for byte and tees every frame to /mirror, so the spectator scene in the iframe watches without taking a second session. Manual — no relay and no agent-client: server.js hands the iframe the real web client, which dials the game server itself under your own Google session.
